Cycling in Tucson

Mount Lemmon, the car-free Loop, dry winter roads

RideRides in Tucson7 routes with a route page each CoffeeCoffee in Tucson6 places · 4 at a ride start FixBike shops in Tucson6 shops · 2 rent bikes StayHotels in Tucson1 with a bike policy in writing · 5 to ask EatRestaurants in Tucson8 places for the night before and after Off the bikeTucson off the bike6 places for the afternoon after Bring the bikeGetting your bike to TucsonFly, ship or rent. Getting around. The rules.

Tucson is the winter riding town. A 28-mile paved climb up Mount Lemmon from the desert floor to the pines; Pima County's car-free Loop, a 54-mile circuit, more than 138 miles of path in all; dry, mild roads from October to April. The fast group ride, the Shootout (Saturdays, 7:00 am), leaves University and Euclid by the university, and GABA posts a social road ride most days of the week. Fly into TUS, eight miles south of downtown. Fair Wheel Bikes rents carbon road bikes and an aluminum gravel bike, Pima Street Bicycle builds a shipped one, and The Tuxon puts bike storage in writing. El Tour de Tucson, the Saturday before Thanksgiving, is the big ride.

Best months
October to April, when the roads are dry and the days are mild. Summer highs run near 100 F from June through August. In summer Pima County says to ride the Loop before 9 a.m. or after 5 p.m. The top of Mount Lemmon runs 20 to 30 F colder than town, with ice in the shade from December to February. Winter storms close the road.
Nearest airport
Tucson International Airport (TUS), 8 mi
Major airport
Phoenix Sky Harbor International (PHX), 112 mi

Clubs and collectives in Tucson

  1. Greater Arizona Bicycling Association (GABA)

    No-drop

    The oldest and largest club in Southern Arizona, in its own words. Leaders post road rides on its Gatherist page most days of the week, from easy social rides (Some Tuesdays, 7:00 am) at 12 to 14 mph to the north-side NW rides (Some Thursdays and Saturdays, 7:00 am) at 14 to 16 mph, which the leaders call no-drop. It also posts El Tour training rides (Sundays, 6:45 am) in the 11 weeks before the race. Rides cap at about 15, so sign up first; the posts ask riders to join GABA ($25 a year, Oct 2026). Its Bike Swap is Sunday, Nov 15, 2026, 7 am to 1 pm, in the El Con Center lot at 3601 E Broadway.

    In the directory: GABA NW Social Rides (Some Thursdays and Saturdays, 7:00 am) →

  2. Cactus Cycling Club

    A road club running mostly B-level rides, 15 to 17 mph, from starts that move around the valley: the Oro Valley ride (Wednesdays, 8:00 am), the Saguaro East loop (Fridays, 7:30 am) and the weekend B rides (Saturdays and Sundays, 7:30 am), most with a coffee or brunch stop after. You must be a member to register, so a visitor takes the free Trial membership (one ride a year), signs the waiver and registers on the club's site first. The club cancels for weather by email.

    In the directory: Friday Saguaro East Ride (Fridays, 7:30 am) →

  3. BICAS

    Women / trans / femme

    The nonprofit community bike shop at 2001 N 7th Ave, under 2 miles north of downtown. They don't fix your bike; they give you a stand, the tools and a mechanic's help to do it yourself, $6 to $12 an hour on a sliding scale, $30 to $60 for the day (Oct 2026). Its rentals are single-speed coaster-brake town bikes, $8 a day (Oct 2026), not for the road. Open Thursday to Sunday, 11 am to 6 pm, per its homepage; Mondays 3 to 7 pm are the Women, Trans and Femme Workshop, with the tools free that night, and the monthly WTF ride (Last Monday of the month, 6:30 pm) leaves after it. BICAS says it is at risk of closing or pausing for lack of money, so call 520-628-7950 before you go.

    In the directory: BICAS WTF Ride (Last Monday of the month, 6:30 pm) →

  4. FUGA (Familias Unidas Ganando Accesibilidad)

    Runs two free monthly community rides, posted in English and Spanish: Bicis y Burros (2nd Sunday of the month, 8:00 am) from the Ward 1 Office on the west side and Bicicleteada del Sur (Last Friday of the month, 6:00 pm) from El Pueblo Center on the south side. No bike? FUGA reserves a Tugo bike share for free: 520-261-5446. Free bike repair once a month at the Ward 1 Office, 940 W Alameda St.

    In the directory: Bicis y Burros (Westside Second Sunday Ride) (2nd Sunday of the month, 8:00 am) →

  5. Sonoran Desert Mountain Bicyclists (SDMB)

    The mountain bike club: it builds and looks after the singletrack around Tucson with Pima County, Marana, the city and the Coronado National Forest. No weekly ride; its public calendar has fall trail work days at Sweetwater, Tucson Mountain Park and Fantasy Island, a Thirsty Thursday at a bar most months, and an all-ladies skills clinic on Oct 24, 2026 at the new 100-Acre Wood Bike Park, 2801 S Alvernon Way.

How Tucson rides: the zones, getting here

About Tucson

Tucson sits on an alluvial plain in the Sonoran Desert at about 2,400 feet, about 60 miles north of the Mexican border. The Santa Catalina Mountains are to the north and the Santa Ritas to the south. It began as a Spanish fort in 1775, was the territorial capital from 1867 to 1877, and is home to the University of Arizona and Davis-Monthan Air Force Base. It is Arizona's second-largest city, about 543,000 people, 110 miles southeast of Phoenix.

The city is known for its food: UNESCO named it the first City of Gastronomy in the United States in 2015. Downtown, Fourth Avenue and the Mercado San Agustín district west of the river hold most of the restaurants and small hotels a visiting rider will use. The Tucson Convention Center, where El Tour starts, sits at the south end of downtown. Summers are hot, with average highs near 100 F from June through August. The rest of the year is mild and dry, which is why the riding runs from fall through spring.

This guide names its zones. Mount Lemmon and the Catalina Highway, northeast of town, with the Tanque Verde Road shop and café at the bottom. The Loop and the west side: the Santa Cruz River path, the Mercado San Agustín, and the Rillito path north of the university. Saguaro National Park East and Old Spanish Trail to the southeast, toward Vail. The Tucson Mountains and Gates Pass to the west. Oro Valley and Catalina State Park to the north. Green Valley, Sahuarita and Madera Canyon to the south. The listings say which side of town they sit on.

Riding in Tucson

The climb is the Catalina Highway up Mount Lemmon: 27.8 miles and about 6,770 feet of climbing (Bike Mount Lemmon) from mile marker 0 to the observatory. No water until the Bigelow trailhead past mile 19, and a top that runs 20 to 30 F colder than the bottom. The ride for the day you land is the Loop: Pima County's paved, car-free path along the Santa Cruz, the Rillito and the washes. A 54-mile circuit you can join anywhere and turn around on. Saguaro National Park East has an 8-mile paved loop through the cactus forest. Gates Pass and the McCain Loop are the west side's climb. Sweetwater Preserve is the singletrack about seven miles from downtown. El Tour de Tucson's 102-mile course runs out Old Spanish Trail past the park and through Vail, Sahuarita and Green Valley.

The group rides are the way in. The Shootout (Saturdays, 7:00 am) leaves University and Euclid by the university and heads south past San Xavier at race pace; the Tuesday Morning Fast Ride (Tuesdays, 6:30 am) leaves the same corner. The Women's Shootout (Saturdays, 7:15 am) leaves the Mercado San Agustín. GABA, the big club, posts no-drop social rides on the north side (Some Thursdays and Saturdays, 7:00 am) and an easier social ride (Some Tuesdays, 7:00 am), much of it on the Loop. Cactus Cycling Club rides B-pace loops in Oro Valley (Wednesdays, 8:00 am), around Saguaro East (Fridays, 7:30 am) and the weekend B rides (Saturdays and Sundays, 7:30 am) from starts that change by the week. FUGA's free community rides, Bicis y Burros (2nd Sunday of the month, 8:00 am) and Bicicleteada del Sur (Last Friday of the month, 6:00 pm), are posted in English and Spanish. BICAS's women, trans and femme ride (Last Monday of the month, 6:30 pm) leaves the co-op after its WTF workshop night. Cyclovia Tucson (Some Sundays, 9:00 am) closes a few miles of streets to cars twice a year.

Getting to Tucson

Fly into Tucson International (TUS), about eight miles south of downtown: Alaska, American, Delta, Southwest, Sun Country and United (Oct 2026), nonstops to about a dozen cities year-round. The Rental Car Center is a walk out the terminal's east exit, and Uber and Lyft pick up on the first island across from baggage claim. Phoenix Sky Harbor is about 112 miles northwest up I-10, the fallback when TUS fares or routes don't work. Groome runs a shared shuttle between the two, but nothing published says it takes a bike box. With a case, a one-way rental car down I-10 is the plain answer. Downtown is walkable and the fare-free Sun Link streetcar carries bikes between the Mercado, downtown, Fourth Avenue and the university. The Bring-your-bike page has the airline rules, the shops that build a shipped bike and the rentals.

Questions about riding in Tucson

Should I bring my bike to Tucson?

Yes, for a week; rent for a day or two. American checks a packed bike under 50 lb as an ordinary bag, $45 each way paid online (Oct 2026), and Southwest, Delta and Alaska do the same at $45 (read Sept 2026). Pima Street Bicycle in midtown receives a shipped bike and builds it for $100 (Oct 2026). Fair Wheel Bikes rents carbon road bikes from $100 a day and gravel from $75 (Oct 2026), so a short trip can go without the case.

When is the best time to ride in Tucson?

October to April. Summer highs run near 100 F from June through August, and Pima County says to ride the Loop before 9 a.m. or after 5 p.m. then. The top of Mount Lemmon is 20 to 30 F colder than town, with ice in the shade from December to February, and winter storms close the road; Pima County's roads hotline is 520-351-3351.

How long is the Mount Lemmon climb?

27.8 miles and about 6,770 feet of climbing (Bike Mount Lemmon) from mile marker 0 on the Catalina Highway to the observatory at the top, at 4.7 percent on average. There is no water on the climb until the Bigelow trailhead past mile 19; Windy Point at mile 14 has toilets and no water. LeBuzz Caffe at Tanque Verde Road and the Catalina Highway opens at 6 and is 4.5 miles from mile 0.

Where do group rides start in Tucson?

The Shootout (Saturdays, 7:00 am) and the Tuesday Morning Fast Ride (Tuesdays, 6:30 am) leave University Boulevard and Euclid Avenue by the University of Arizona. The Women's Shootout (Saturdays, 7:15 am) leaves the Mercado San Agustín west of downtown. GABA's NW social rides (Some Thursdays and Saturdays, 7:00 am) start at St. Philip's Plaza or at Bruegger's in Oro Valley, and its social ride (Some Tuesdays, 7:00 am) moves each week; sign up on Gatherist first. Cactus Cycling Club's rides take a free trial membership.

Can I rent a road bike in Tucson?

Yes. Fair Wheel Bikes on 6th Street rents aluminum road from $65, carbon Shimano 105 from $100, Di2 from $115, ENVE with SRAM AXS from $135, a Trek Checkpoint gravel bike from $75 and mountain bikes from $65 for the first day, pedals of your choice included (Oct 2026). Earlybird Bikes rents road, gravel and mountain bikes at the foot of Mount Lemmon, prices in its booking system. Tucson Bicycle Rentals rents carbon road bikes from pickup points at $125 a day or $395 a week, no walk-ins (Oct 2026). For El Tour, book early.

Do I need a car to ride in Tucson?

Not if you stay central. The Shootout start, Fair Wheel's rental fleet and the Loop are within a mile or so of downtown, and the Mount Lemmon climb is a ride away: LeBuzz at the bottom is about 11 miles northeast. The fare-free Sun Link streetcar carries bikes between the Mercado, downtown, Fourth Avenue and the university. You will want a car, or an XL ride, for the airport leg with a bike case and for the far trailheads.
